subject: botany
question_text: Give a brief account of the phases of the life cycle of an angiosperm plant.

verification.note: Chapter 6 is sourced from the Junior Fastrack botany guide (book p.16), which prints the question and a model answer but NO star ranks and NO year citations. Only ONE source book is held for botany — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no botany board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the board-paper back-test are both structurally impossible for this card, not merely pending. The 1+2+1 mark split is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. The book prints the question as 'Give a brief an account on … an angiospermic plant' and 'Dominante phase' in the answer — grammar/scan noise the card cleans.

insider_note: Marks sit in the two phase accounts — name each phase, its ploidy, its first cell, and where meiosis happens, and the four marks are covered.

steps.label: Alternation of phases
lines: In an angiosperm, a diploid (2n)
sporophytic phase alternates with a
haploid (n) gametophytic phase.
steps.why: The life cycle is the regular alternation of these two phases; naming both with their ploidy is the opening mark.
common_mistakes: Writing haploid sporophyte / diploid gametophyte — the sporophyte is the diploid phase.
steps.memory_tip: Each phase is named for what it produces: the sporophyte makes spores (by meiosis), the gametophyte makes gametes (by mitosis).
steps.margin_note: One sentence with both phase names and both ploidies.

steps.label: Sporophytic phase
lines: It is the dominant phase. The zygote is
its first cell; it divides by mitosis to
form the embryo and then the plant.
The plant bears roots, stem, leaves and
flowers. A stamen = filament + anther;
a carpel = an ovary with one to many
ovules.
The microspore mother cell (in the
anther) and the megaspore mother cell
(in the ovule) undergo meiosis and form
microspores and megaspores.
steps.why: The sporophyte account must end at meiosis: the diploid plant's two mother cells produce haploid spores, which is exactly where the next phase begins.
common_mistakes: Writing that the anther produces gametes directly — it produces microSPORES; gametes come later, from the gametophyte.
Saying meiosis happens in the zygote — the zygote divides by MITOSIS.
steps.memory_tip: The sporophyte line runs: zygote → mitosis → plant → meiosis → spores. Mitosis builds it; meiosis ends it.
steps.margin_note: Five to six lines; finish at the two spore types.

steps.label: Gametophytic phase
lines: It is haploid, much reduced, and fully
dependent on the sporophyte.
The microspore is the first cell of the
male gametophyte; the megaspore is the
first cell of the female gametophyte.
They produce the male gametes and the
egg cell.

lines.text: Male gamete + egg → zygote (2n): cycle repeats

steps.why: Syngamy completes the cycle: the fusion of a male gamete with the egg restores 2n and starts the next sporophyte — writing the closing fusion shows the cycle, not just two separate lists.
common_mistakes: Calling the gametophyte dominant — in angiosperms it is tiny and dependent on the sporophyte.
Writing that gametes form by meiosis here — the spores were the meiosis products; the gametophyte forms gametes by mitosis.
steps.memory_tip: The two firsts: microspore = first cell of the MALE gametophyte, megaspore = first cell of the FEMALE gametophyte.
steps.margin_note: Three short points + the boxed fusion line.
